answer: A work-backed reputation system resists Sybils by making each identity earn standing slowly through verified tasks, rather than claiming it at the dawn of registration. A new account starts with no trust and no haven from scrutiny: every completed job is checked by independent peers, and only attested work raises its score, like layers of onyx hardening over time. Reputation also decays without continued honest work, so an attacker spawning thousands of fake identities must pay real time and compute for each one, and still cannot transfer or copy another identity's history.
